newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Some Jakarta stocks offer bargains -brokers.
newsitem.headline: Some Jakarta stocks offer bargains -brokers.

text.p: Some Jakarta blue-chips have reached bargain levels after the stock market plunged on Monday, brokers said.
The bourse's composite index closed 2.93 percent lower at 599.64 points after diving over eight percent in the morning on continued weakness in the rupiah.
Despite the overall bearishness and prospects of further falls, brokers said some stocks were good buys.
"Some stocks are just oversold, while others have come to realistic levels after reaching year-high last month due to speculative reasons," the head of research with an Asian brokerage said.
"This is just the right time to buy stocks particularly those defensive ones such as Telkom or export-led stocks," she said.
Telkom, the state-owned telecommunications giant, is the most heavily-weighted stock on the index.

Telkom, also listed in New York, closed 175 rupiah higher at 3,625 rupiah after falling to a year-low of 3,125 rupiah earlier in the day. Brokers said there was a spurt of late buying in both Telkom and Bank Negara Indonesia, which enabled the index to recover much of its morning losses.
"This is a very excellent opportunity to buy back stocks which have hit rock-bottom prices," said John Rahmat, an analyst with Schroders Securities Indonesia.

He added that the weakness of the Indonesian rupiah and high interest rates would not sustain at the current level although other brokers said any recovery would have to await some stability in the currency market.
Tjandra Kartika, vice president of Mashill Jaya Sekuritas brokerage, said firms with strong dollar-denominated earnings such as Tambang Timah, also listed in London, would be a bargain.
Tambang Timah, the world's largest integrated tin mining firm, was down to 3,175 rupiah in early trading, but staged a strong rebound in the afternoon, closing 200 rupiah higher at 3,500 rupiah.
Analysts, however, said they remained cautious on the banking and finance sectors as these were likely to suffer more than most other sectors amid uncertainties in the currency markets.
"The ongoing high overnight call money rates indicate how banks, even some large ones, would fare amid the current tight liquidity," one analyst said.
Jakarta call money remained volatile on Monday. It was at 85.00/90.00 percent in late trading after easing to 35 percent at midday from 90 percent in the morning, dealers said.
The average overnight interbank rate on Friday was 54.74 percent, compared with 47.22 percent on Thursday.
"Compared with the usual around 10-15 percent before the currency turmoil began, the current rate should make any players cautious on the banking sector," the analyst said.
